leading_indicator_description: Vibration velocity climbs steadily above the normal envelope over roughly a week before failure.
Tool wear approaches its limit during the final hours of tool life.
Vibration rises sharply and across a broad band over about three days as the spindle bearing degrades.
Spindle temperature trends upward through the day preceding thermal overload.
Torque readings become erratic as belt tension is progressively lost over about five days.
Temperature drifts upward over two days as lubricant delivery falls below requirement.
No leading indicator; an instrumentation fault appears without measurable warning.
Power draw rises and becomes unstable over about four days before the drive fails.
No leading indicator; a controller fault presents abruptly.
Compressed air pressure falls below the normal envelope in the hours before the fault.
Power draw drifts upward over roughly ten days as belt tension and alignment degrade.
No leading indicator; a blockage produces an immediate step change in load.
Power draw increases slowly over about two weeks as roller bearings wear.
